rules.source_section: INDICATIONS FOR LOWER EXTREMITY MRI / Joint Specific Pain or Suspected Joint Specific Injury
rules.source_quote: Joint Specific Pain or Suspected Joint Specific Injury
rules.clinical_service_or_procedure: Lower Extremity MRI (Knee, Hip, Ankle, Foot)

criteria.description: Evaluation of joint-specific pain, mechanical locking, instability, or suspected internal derangement (ligament/meniscal tear)

required_documentation: Physical examination documenting joint effusion, mechanical locking, McMurray, Lachman, or joint line tenderness and initial X-ray report
rules.review_notes: Standard lower extremity joint MRI for internal derangement.

rules.source_section: INDICATIONS FOR LOWER EXTREMITY MRI / Joint Specific Orthopedic Signs
rules.source_quote: Joint specific advanced imaging is indicated for any positive orthopedic sign listed below:

criteria.description: Physical examination demonstrates positive joint-specific sign for meniscal or ligamentous tear (e.g. McMurray test, joint line tenderness, Lachman test, anterior/posterior drawer, pivot shift)
Prior plain radiograph completed showing no clear explanation for mechanical symptoms or acute fracture

required_documentation: Orthopedic physical examination documenting specific positive knee exam signs and plain radiograph report
rules.review_notes: With positive orthopedic knee exam signs, active conservative therapy is waived.

rules.source_section: INDICATIONS FOR LOWER EXTREMITY MRI / OSTEONECROSIS

criteria.description: Clinical suspicion of osteonecrosis / avascular necrosis (AVN) of the femoral head with risk factors (e.g. chronic steroid therapy, sickle cell disease, alcoholism) and normal or inconclusive plain radiographs

required_documentation: Clinical notes detailing hip pain, AVN risk factors, and negative/indeterminate plain radiographs
rules.review_notes: MRI is the most sensitive diagnostic modality for early avascular necrosis of the hip.
